Viral load outcomes are reported for the following time points: the last available VL <12 months before ("pretransition VL"), the VL at 12 months after (window: 6--18 months; ≥6 months before the 24-month VL; "12-month VL"), and the VL at 24 months (window: 18--30 months; "24-month VL") after transition to DTG. If multiple VLs were recorded within the window for the 12- or 24-month VL, the measurement closest to 12 or 24 months, respectively, was selected. In addition, we report the last available VL both before and after transition to DTG, regardless of time window. VLs are categorized as <50 copies/mL, 50--999 copies/mL, >999 copies/mL, or missing.

Participant characteristics and VL outcomes are summarized as frequency and percentage for categorical data and median and interquartile range (IQR) for continuous data, and are reported stratified by the pretransition VL. Determinants of 24-month viremia ≥50 copies/mL were assessed among participants with 24-month VLs using logistic regression models. The same analyses were performed combining pretransition VL and backbone change to a single variable to address potential collinearity, and among the subgroups with a pretransition VL <50 copies/mL or ≥50 copies/mL. Upon observing an association of both a viremic and missing pretransition VLs with 24-month viremia, we simulated the expected effect size of a missing pretransition VL assuming that any effect was driven exclusively by undocumented viremia occurring at the same rate as documented viremia (see Supplementary Material section F), and compared the simulated with the observed effect size.
